    Restricted marketable investments of $3.0&#160;million and
    $8.7&#160;million at December&#160;31, 2006 and 2005,
    respectively, consist of United States government agency
    investments and relate to the issuance of convertible debt in
    March 2004.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 3%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In September 2004, we acquired four million shares of SuperGen,
    Inc. (&#147;SuperGen&#148;) as part of a transaction that
    included obtaining the worldwide licensing rights for Dacogen.
    The investment is accounted for as long-term available for sale
    marketable securities. As such, unrealized gains and losses have
    been reported in accumulated other comprehensive income (loss).
    As of June&#160;30, 2006, the fair value of MGI&#146;s
    investment in SuperGen was $14.5&#160;million and had been below
    our cost basis of $24.4&#160;million for over six months. As a
    result, we determined that an
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">other-than-temporary</FONT>
    impairment had occurred and in accordance with SFAS&#160;115
    &#147;Accounting for Certain Investments in Debt and Equity
    Securities&#148;, we recorded an
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">other-than-temporary</FONT>
    impairment charge of $9.9&#160;million in the second quarter of
    2006, which reduced our cost basis to $14.5&#160;million. As of
    December&#160;31, 2006, the fair value of our SuperGen
    investment was $20.3&#160;million.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 3%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In addition to our investment in SuperGen, we also own
    2,181,398&#160;shares of MethylGene. MethylGene completed its
    initial public offering and began trading publicly on the
    Toronto Stock Exchange on June&#160;29, 2004. MGI&#146;s
    carrying value of the MethylGene investment prior to
    MethylGene&#146;s initial public offering was $3.6&#160;million.
    As of December&#160;31, 2006, the fair value of our MethylGene
    investment was $7.7&#160;million.
</DIV>

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">6.&#160;&#160;</FONT></B>

    <TD>
    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Acquisitions</FONT></B>
</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">2005</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On October&#160;3, 2005, Granite Acquisition, Inc., a Delaware
    corporation and wholly owned subsidiary of MGI, merged with and
    into Guilford Pharmaceuticals Inc., a Delaware corporation now
    known as MGI GP, Inc. (&#147;Guilford&#148; or &#147;MGI
    GP&#148;), with Guilford surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary
    of MGI (the &#147;Guilford Merger&#148;). Upon closing of the
    Guilford Merger, all shares of Guilford common stock were
    exchanged for the right to receive an aggregate of approximately
    5.3&#160;million shares of our common stock plus approximately
    $53.9&#160;million in cash, which represented $3.75&#160;per
    Guilford share of common stock, based on the average closing
    price of our common stock over a five trading day period ended
    on September&#160;27, 2005, or total consideration of
    $176.1&#160;million to Gulford shareholders. The transaction has
    been accounted for as a purchase business combination.
    Commencing October&#160;3, 2005, the results of Guilford&#146;s
    operations have been included in our consolidated financial
    statements.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In connection with the Guilford merger, we extinguished
    Guilford&#146;s revenue interest assignment agreement with Paul
    Royalty Fund, L.P. and Paul Royalty Fund,&#160;II, L.P.
    (collectively, &#147;PRF&#148;) for $59.9&#160;million.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Guilford Merger triggered an obligation for us to make an
    offer to repurchase all of Guilford&#146;s 5%&#160;Convertible
    Subordinated Notes due July&#160;1, 2008 (the &#147;Guilford
    Notes&#148;) in accordance with the terms of the related
    indenture at a repurchase price in cash equal to 100% of the
    principal amount of the Notes, plus accrued and unpaid interest
    and liquidated damages, if any, up to but excluding the payment
    date. Each $1,000 principal amount of the Notes was convertible,
    at the option of the holder, into (i)&#160;17.6772&#160;shares
    of our common stock, and (ii)&#160;$180.28 in cash through
    November&#160;28, 2005. At the expiration of the offer to
    repurchase, we had repurchased $69.2&#160;million of the
    Guilford Notes. The remaining $1.5&#160;million of the Guilford
    Notes were accounted for as debt assumed on the date of
    acquisition. (See Note&#160;10).
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    The purchase price was allocated to the tangible and
    identifiable intangible assets acquired and liabilities assumed
    based on their estimated fair values at the acquisition date. In
    accordance with SFAS&#160;No.&#160;141, the excess of the

    liabilities was allocated to goodwill. The determination of fair
    value requires management to make significant estimates and
    assumptions.

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 3%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The acquired in-process research and development
    (&#147;IPR&#38;D&#148;) included: $156.5&#160;million for
    product candidate compounds under development that have not yet
    achieved regulatory approval for marketing and have no
    alternative future use, and $0.4&#160;million for the exclusive
    option to purchase SNDC. In the second quarter of 2006, we
    effectively terminated the purchse option agreement with SNDC.
    The $156.9&#160;million allocated to IPR&#38;D was immediately
    expensed in the consolidated statement of operations in the
    fourth quarter of 2005. This charge is not deductible for tax
    purposes. The $156.5&#160;million of IPR&#38;D attributable to
    product candidate compounds under development that have not yet
    achieved regulatory approval for marketing and have no
    alternative future use represents 100&#160;percent of the
    estimated fair value of Guilford&#146;s product candidate,
    Aquavan Injection&#160;(&#147;Aquavan&#148;).
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 3%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    There are several methods that can be used to determine the
    estimated fair value of the acquired IPR&#38;D. For Aquavan, we
    utilized the &#147;income method,&#148; which applies a
    probability weighting to the estimated future net cash flows
    that are derived from projected sales revenues and estimated
    costs. These projections are based on factors such as relevant
    market size, patent protection, historical pricing of similar
    products, and expected industry trends. The estimated future net
    cash flows are then discounted to the present value using an
    appropriate discount rate that incorporates the weighted average
    cost of capital relative to our industry and us as well as
    product specific risks associated with the acquired in-process
    research and development products. Product specific risk factors
    include the
</DIV>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <BR>
    87
</DIV><!-- END LOGICAL PAGE -->

    </FONT></B>

    CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL
    STATEMENTS&#160;&#151;&#160;(Continued)</FONT></B>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    product&#146;s phase of development, likelihood of success,
    clinical data, target product profile and development plan. The
    appropriate discount rate was determined to be approximately
    17&#160;percent. We believe the assumptions used in the
    valuation were reasonable at the time of the acquisition.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    To estimate the fair value of the exclusive option to purchase
    SNDC, we used an option pricing model. We believe the

    The major risks and uncertainties associated with the timely and
    successful completion of these projects consist of the ability

    Administration (&#147;FDA&#148;) notified Guilford that Gliadel
    was entitled to market exclusivity for the treatment of patients
    with malignant glioma undergoing primary surgical resection
    until February 2010, under applicable orphan drug laws. In
    addition, Gliadel is manufactured using a proprietary process.
    We believe that this proprietary process will provide a
    significant barrier to future, generic competition. The initial
    estimated fair value of the Aggrastat intangible asset was
    derived using the income method, however, this initial
    allocation was subject to change as we were seeking market
    participant data to complete the purchase price allocation.
    During the third quarter of 2006, we completed the purchase
    price allocation for Guilford related to Aggrastat when MGI sold
    its product rights for Aggrastat to Medicure, Inc. Aggrastat was
    being amortized on a straight-line basis over 5&#160;years from
    the date of acquisition, which was the estimate of the life of
    the product. (See Note&#160;7).

    rate that incorporates the weighted average cost of capital

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <B>Aesgen:</B>&#160;&#160;On September&#160;28, 2004, MGIP
    Acquisition Corp., a Delaware corporation and a wholly owned
    subsidiary of MGI PHARMA, merged with and into Aesgen, a
    Delaware corporation, with Aesgen surviving as our wholly owned
    subsidiary. Aesgen, Inc. was a privately held company focused on
    treating side effects associated with cancer treatments.
    Aesgen&#146;s lead product, Saforis Powder for Oral Suspension
    (&#147;Saforis&#148;), is a phase&#160;3 product candidate in
    development for treatment of oral mucositis. The transaction has
    been accounted for as a purchase business combination.
    Commencing September&#160;28, 2004, the results of Aesgen&#146;s
    operations have been included in our consolidated financial
    statements.
</DIV>

    we paid $32&#160;million in cash at the closing. In addition, we
    assumed $1.1&#160;million in liabilities and incurred
    $1.9&#160;million in transaction fees, including legal,
    valuation and accounting fees.

    based on their estimated fair values at the acquisition date.
    The excess of the fair values of the assets and liabilities over
    the purchase price amounted to $0.5&#160;million and was
    allocated to negative goodwill. In a business combination with
    contingent consideration, the lesser of the maximum amount of
    contingent consideration or the total amount of negative
    goodwill should be recognized as a liability. In this case,
    negative goodwill is less than the maximum amount of contingent
    consideration and as a result, the $0.5&#160;million is
    recognized as a noncurrent liability. The determination of

    estimates and assumptions. The following table summarizes the

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The acquired IPR&#38;D represents product candidate compounds
    under development that have not yet achieved regulatory approval
    for marketing and have no alternative future use. Accordingly,
    the $31.7&#160;million allocated to IPR&#38;D was immediately
    expensed in the consolidated statement of operations in the
    third quarter of 2004. This charge is not deductible for tax
    purposes. Aesgen&#146;s lead product (Saforis), a product
    candidate in development for treatment of oral mucositis,
    represents 100&#160;percent of the estimated fair value of the
    IPR&#38;D.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We utilized the income method to value the estimated IPR&#38;D.
    We applied a probability weighting to the estimated future net
    cash flows that are derived from projected sales revenues and
    estimated costs. These projections were based on factors such as
    relevant market size, patent protection, historical pricing of
    similar products, and expected industry trends. The estimated
    future net cash flows are then discounted to the present value
    using an appropriate discount rate that incorporates the
    weighted average cost of capital relative to our industry and us
    as well as product specific risks associated with the acquired
    in-process research and development products. Product specific
    risk factors included the product&#146;s phase of development,
    likelihood of success, clinical data, target product profile and
    development plan. The appropriate discount rate was determined
    to be approximately 20&#160;percent. We believe the assumptions
    used in the valuation were reasonable at the time of the
    acquisition.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The major risks and uncertainties associated with the timely and
    successful completion of this project consist of the ability to
    confirm the safety and efficacy of the technology based on the
    data from clinical trials and obtaining necessary regulatory
    approvals. In addition, no assurance can be given that the
    underlying assumptions used to forecast the cash flows or the
    timely and successful completion of such project will
    materialize, as estimated. For these reasons, among others,
    actual results may vary significantly from the estimated results.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Technology
    Out-License Arrangements</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Dacogen
    for Injection</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In July 2006, we entered into a license agreement with Cilag
    GmbH, a Johnson&#160;&#38; Johnson company, granting exclusive
    development and commercialization rights for Dacogen in all
    territories outside North America to Janssen-Cilag companies,
    members of the Johnson&#160;&#38; Johnson family of companies.
    MGI and the Janssen-Cilag companies will jointly implement a
    strategic plan for the global clinical development of Dacogen.
    Under the terms of this agreement, we will retain all
    commercialization rights to Dacogen in North America.
    Janssen-Cilag companies will be responsible for conducting
    regulatory and commercial activities related to Dacogen in all
    territories outside North America, while we retain
    responsibility for all activities in the United States, Canada
    and Mexico. Pursuant to the terms of this agreement, we received
    from Cilag GmbH an upfront payment of $10&#160;million and may
    earn milestone payments totaling more than $37&#160;million
    should all specified clinical development, regulatory, and
    commercial goals be achieved. Under the terms of the Dacogen
    license agreement between us and SuperGen, Inc., we will share
    these upfront and milestone payments from Cilag GmbH with
    SuperGen. In addition to the previously described payments, in
    the three years from the date of the agreement, we will receive
    from Cilag GmbH research and development support totaling
    $25&#160;million, of which $18&#160;million will be cash and
    $7&#160;million may be cash or services, related to specified
    clinical development activities, of which $6&#160;million had
    been received as of December&#160;31, 2006. We will receive a
    royalty from Cilag GmbH on net sales of Dacogen in each of the
    countries covered by this agreement, which we will also share
    with SuperGen.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Salagen
    Tablets</FONT></I></B>

    In September 2004, we obtained exclusive worldwide rights to the
    development, commercialization, manufacturing and distribution
    of Dacogen for all indications from SuperGen. Dacogen is an
    anti-cancer therapeutic approved by the FDA on May&#160;2, 2006
    for the treatment of patients with myelodysplastic syndrome
    (&#147;MDS&#148;). In addition to the clinically proven activity
    of Dacogen in patients with MDS, data from phase&#160;1 and 2
    trials suggest that Dacogen may be active in a variety of other
    hematological malignancies such as acute myeloid leukemia
    (&#147;AML&#148;). A pivotal program in patients with AML was
    initiated in 2005. Under the terms of our agreement with
    SuperGen, we paid $40.0&#160;million to SuperGen and we incurred
    $1.1&#160;million of transaction fees, including legal and
    accounting fees. We received four million shares of SuperGen
    that were valued at $24.4&#160;million on the purchase date and
    are reported as an
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">available-for-sale</FONT>
    equity security. (See Note&#160;2 for discussion on changes in
    the value of our SuperGen investment). The difference between
    total consideration ($41.1&#160;million) and the fair value of
    the equity investment ($24.4&#160;million) of $16.7&#160;million
    was recorded as research and development expense in the third
    quarter of 2004. We have met our commitment to SuperGen to fund
    at least $15.0&#160;million of further Dacogen development costs
    as of December&#160;31, 2005. We expensed a total of
    $12.5&#160;million in milestone obligations during 2004 for:
    (1)&#160;the filing of the NDA for Dacogen with the FDA and
    (2)&#160;a Marketing Authorization Application (&#147;MAA&#148;)
    filing with the EMEA. In the second quarter of 2006, we paid to
    SuperGen a milestone payment of $20&#160;million for the first
    commercial sale of Dacogen in the United States. This amount was
    capitalized as an intangible asset because FDA approval had been
    received for Dacogen prior to the payment. We expect to make
    additional milestone payments totaling $12.5&#160;million upon
    achievement of regulatory and commercialization milestones in
    Europe and Japan. Subject to certain limitations, we will also
    pay SuperGen 50&#160;percent of certain revenue payable as a
    result of our sublicensing rights to market, sell or distribute
    Dacogen, to the extent such revenues are in excess of the
    milestone payments. In addition, SuperGen will receive a royalty
    on annual worldwide net sales of licensed product starting at
    20&#160;percent and escalating to a maximum of 30&#160;percent.
    For the year ended December&#160;31, 2006, we recognized

    On March&#160;2, 2004, we issued $348&#160;million of senior
    subordinated convertible notes, (&#147;the Notes&#148;). The net
    proceeds to us were $252.1&#160;million after discount of
    $87.8&#160;million and issuance costs of $8.1&#160;million. We
    will pay cash interest on the Notes at the rate of
    1.6821&#160;percent per year on the principal amount at maturity
    (2.25&#160;percent per year of the issue price) payable
    semiannually from September&#160;2, 2004 until March&#160;2,
    2011. After March&#160;2, 2011, we will not pay cash interest on
    the Notes prior to maturity at March&#160;2, 2024 and we will
    begin to amortize the discount

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Notes are convertible at the option of the holders into
    shares of our common stock only under the following
    circumstances: (1)&#160;if the closing sale price of our common
    stock was more than 120&#160;percent of the then current
    conversion price of the Notes for at least 20 trading days in
    the period of the 30 consecutive trading days ending on the last
    trading day of the previous calendar quarter (once the foregoing
    condition is satisfied for any one quarter, then the Notes will
    thereafter be convertible at any time at the option of the
    holder, through maturity), (2)&#160;if we elect to redeem the
    Notes, (3)&#160;upon the occurrence of specified corporate
    transactions or if significant distributions to holders of our
    common stock occur or (4)&#160;subject to certain exceptions,
    for the five consecutive business day period following any five
    consecutive trading day period in which the average trading
    price of the Notes was less than 98&#160;percent of the average
    of the sale price of our common stock during such
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">five-day</FONT>
    trading period multiplied by the Notes then current conversion
    rate. Subject to the above conditions, the Notes are convertible
    into an aggregate of 8,269,942&#160;shares of common stock at an
    initial conversion price of $31.46&#160;per share of common
    stock.

    Merger triggered an obligation for MGI PHARMA to make an offer

    of the Notes, plus accrued and unpaid interest and liquidated
    damages, if any, up to but excluding the payment date. At the
    expiration of the offer to repurchase and at December&#160;31,
    2006, $1.5&#160;million of the Guilford Notes were outstanding.
    Interest on the Guilford Notes accrues at 5%&#160;per annum and
    is payable semi-annually on January 1 and July&#160;1 each year,
    commencing on January&#160;1, 2004. The Guilford Notes are
    convertible, at the option of the holder at any time prior to
    maturity, into (i)&#160;17.6772&#160;shares of MGI PHARMA common
    stock, and (ii)&#160;$180.28 in cash per each $1,000 aggregate
    principal amount at maturity. We have the option to redeem the
    Notes on or after July&#160;6, 2006 for 102.00% of the principal
    amount through July&#160;6, 2007 and thereafter through maturity
    at 101.00% of the principal amount.

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">11.&#160;&#160;</FONT></B>
</TD>
    <TD>
    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Revolving
    Credit Facility</FONT></B>
</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On October&#160;18, 2006, we entered into a three year credit
    agreement and related security agreements to provide financing
    for up to $75&#160;million, subject to a borrowing base. The
    borrowing base equals the sum of 85% of the aggregate face
    amount of our eligible accounts receivable (net of certain
    chargeback reserves and distribution fees), less certain defined
    reserves. The revolving credit facility provides that we have
    the right at any time to request up to $25&#160;million of
    additional commitments under this facility. If we were to
    request any such additional commitments and the existing lenders
    or new lenders were to agree to provide such commitments, the
    facility size could be increased to up to $100&#160;million, but
    our ability to borrow under this facility would still be limited
    by the amount of the borrowing base.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Borrowings under the revolving credit facility bear interest at
    a rate equal to, at our option, either (a)&#160;a base rate
    determined by reference to the higher of (1)&#160;Chase&#146;s
    prime lending rate and (2)&#160;the federal funds effective rate
    plus 0.5% or (b)&#160;a Eurodollar rate (LIBOR) determined by
    reference to the costs of funds for U.S.&#160;dollar deposits in
    the London interbank market for the interest period relevant to
    such borrowing adjusted for certain additional costs, in each
    case plus an applicable margin. The applicable margin for
    borrowings under our new revolving credit facility ranges from
    0.00% to 0.25% for base rate borrowings and 0.75% to 1.75% for
    Eurodollar borrowings, subject to adjustment based on our
    average liquidity, calculated as set forth in the Credit
    Agreement.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In addition to paying interest on outstanding principal under
    our new revolving credit facility, we are required to pay a
    commitment fee of 0.125%&#160;per annum in respect of the
    unutilized commitments thereunder. We must also pay customary
    letter of credit fees and agency fees. As of December&#160;31,
    2006, there were no borrowings under this revolving credit
    facility.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

    share purchase right (&#147;Right&#148;). Each Right entitles
    the registered holder to purchase one one-hundredth of a share

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Under our stock incentive plans, designated persons (including
    officers, directors, employees, licensors and consultants) have
    been or may be granted rights to acquire our common stock. These
    rights include stock options, restricted stock units and other
    equity rights. Stock options become exercisable over varying
    periods, generally four years, and generally expire up to seven
    years from the date of grant. Options may be granted in the form
    of incentive stock options or nonqualified stock options. When
    options are exercised, shares are issued from our authorized
    shares. At our May&#160;9, 2006 Annual Meeting of Shareholders,
    the shareholders approved the addition of 7.4&#160;million
    shares to the 1997 Plan. At December&#160;31, 2006, shares
    issued and shares available under stock incentive plans are as
    follows:

<DIV align="center" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">MGI
    PHARMA, INC.<BR>

</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">NOTES&#160;TO
    CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL
    STATEMENTS&#160;&#151;&#160;(Continued)</FONT></B>

<P>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    As part of the Guilford acquisition (see Note&#160;6), we
    assumed the 2002 Plan. At the time we assumed the 2002 Plan, no
    stock awards were outstanding and 818,349&#160;shares were
    available for grant. A total of 797,326 stock awards were
    granted from the 2002 Plan in 2005, of which 709,576 were stock
    options that were granted at an average price of $23.08.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Prior to January&#160;1, 2006, the following methods and
    assumptions were used to determine the fair value of options
    granted. Options were priced based on the closing price of a
    share of our common stock at the date of grant. The fair value
    of each option grant was estimated on the date of grant using
    the Black-Scholes option-pricing model. To determine the inputs
    for the Black-Scholes option pricing model we used the
    historical volatility of our stock to estimate expected
    volatility and the period of time that option grants were
    expected to be outstanding. The risk-free rate was based on the
    U.S.&#160;Treasury yield curve in effect at the time of grant
    for the estimated life of the option. The adoption of
    SFAS&#160;No.&#160;123R did not change our accounting for
    restricted stock units.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">NOTES&#160;TO

    STATEMENTS&#160;&#151;&#160;(Continued)</FONT></B>
</DIV>
<P>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Restricted
    Stock Units</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    For the years ended December&#160;31, 2006, 2005 and 2004, we
    issued 484,628, 273,699 and 141,422 restricted stock units,
    respectively, to designated persons. The vesting periods vary up
    to four years, given continued employment through the vesting
    dates. We calculate compensation expense for the market value of
    the shares at the date of grant and recognize the expense over
    the vesting periods. As of December&#160;31, 2006, 63,546
    restricted stock units had been cancelled, and
    179,552&#160;shares vested of which 46,327 were subsequently
    exchanged and cancelled for the minimum statutory tax
    withholding requirements of the employee.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><U><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Employee
    Stock Purchase Plan</FONT></U></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    As of January&#160;1, 2006, substantially all employees may
    purchase shares of common stock at the end of quarterly purchase
    periods at a price equal to 85&#160;percent of the stock&#146;s
    closing market price on the last business day of each calendar
    quarter. Plan funding will occur throughout the purchase period
    by pre-elected payroll deductions of up to 15&#160;percent of
    regular pay. In accordance with SFAS&#160;No.&#160;123R, we
    record as compensation expense an amount equal to the
    15&#160;percent discount given to employees. The compensation
    expense recorded for the year ended December&#160;31, 2006 was
    $0.3&#160;million. Shares issued under the plan were 112,257 at
    an average price of $15.78&#160;per share in 2006. At
    December&#160;31, 2006, 1,384,182&#160;shares remain reserved
    for future issuance under the plan.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Prior to January&#160;1, 2006, under our employee stock purchase
    plan, substantially all employees were allowed to purchase
    shares of common stock at the end of semi-annual purchase
    periods at a price equal to the lower of 85&#160;percent of the
    stock&#146;s fair market value on the first or last day of that
    period. Plan funding occured throughout the purchase period by
    pre-elected payroll deductions of up to 15&#160;percent of
    regular pay. In accordance with APB Opinion No.&#160;25,
    &#147;Accounting for Stock Issued to Employees&#148;, no
    compensation expense resulted from the plan in 2004 and 2005.
    Shares issued under the plan were 91,892 and 66,011 at average
    prices of $16.42 and $20.17&#160;per share in 2005 and 2004,
    respectively.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><U><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Retirement
    Plan</FONT></U></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Participation in our retirement plan is available to
    substantially all employees. Participants may elect to
    contribute a percentage of their eligible compensation
    consistent with Section&#160;401(k) of the Internal Revenue Code
    and we make contributions that are a portion of participant
    contributions and a percentage of their eligible compensation.
    In addition, we may make discretionary contributions ratably to
    all eligible employees. Our contributions are made in cash or
    our common stock and become fully vested when a participant
    attains five years of service. Participants may direct
    investment of contributions into any of the plan&#146;s
    investment alternatives, but contributions made in the form of
    our common stock must be fully vested before redirection can
    occur. Total retirement plan contribution expense was
    $3.6&#160;million, $4.0&#160;million and $3.3&#160;million in
    2006, 2005 and 2004, respectively, of which $2.9&#160;million,
    $2.4&#160;million and $2.1&#160;million was made in our common
    stock in 2006, 2005 and 2004, respectively. We had
    708,765&#160;shares reserved for future issuance under the
    retirement plan at December&#160;31, 2006.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><U><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Preferred
    Stock</FONT></U></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    At December&#160;31, 2006, we had 10,000,000 authorized and
    unissued shares of preferred stock. Issuance is subject to
    action by our board of directors.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The SNDC and PIPE warrants are classified as liabilities and
    measured at fair value, with changes in fair value reported in
    earnings. The classification of these warrants as liabilities is
    due to required net-cash settlement by MGI PHARMA on the
    occurrence of certain events outside the control of MGI. On the
    date of acquisition, the fair value of these warrants was
    $1.1&#160;million and at December&#160;31, 2006 and 2005 the
    fair value was $0.3&#160;million and $0.5&#160;million,
    respectively. The differences of $0.2&#160;million and
    $0.6&#160;million were reported in other income for the years
    ended December&#160;31, 2006 and 2005, respectively.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We maintain a valuation allowance to reserve against our
    deferred tax assets due to uncertainty over the ability to
    realize these deferred tax benefits. As of December&#160;31,
    2006 and 2005, the valuation allowances were $285.7&#160;million
    and $256.0&#160;million, respectively. Of these amounts,
    $31.6&#160;million as of December&#160;31, 2006, and
    $28.7&#160;million as of December&#160;31, 2005, were
    attributable to the exercise of stock options. These amounts
    will be recorded as an increase to additional paid-in capital if
    it is determined in the future that this portion of the
    valuation allowance is no longer required.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    As part of the Guilford acquisition in 2005, we acquired
    $118.2&#160;million of deferred tax assets consisting of
    $61.1&#160;million in income tax net operating loss
    carryforwards, $0.9&#160;million in state research and
    development tax credit carryforwards, other tax assets of
    $56.5&#160;million and deferred tax liabilities of $0.3 along
    with the associated valuation allowance to fully reserve against
    those deferred tax assets due to the uncertainty over the
    ability to realize the acquired deferred tax benefits.
</DIV>

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">17.&#160;&#160;</FONT></B>
</TD>
    <TD>
    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Restructuring</FONT></B>
</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On October&#160;24, 2006, we implemented a plan of
    organizational restructuring (the &#147;Plan&#148;, approved by
    management on October&#160;20, 2006)&#160;in order to better
    align our workforce and resources with our operational
    objectives. Under the Plan, we expect to lower our cost
    structure by (i)&#160;reducing total workforce by approximately
    10%, or 56 positions, (ii)&#160;consolidating drug development
    functions at one location, (iii)&#160;in connection with that
    consolidation, relocating up to approximately 35 positions, and
    (iv)&#160;consolidating our Baltimore operations from two
    facilities to one facility.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We estimate that, under the Plan, we will incur approximately
    $3.8&#160;million of costs for severance benefits. As of
    December&#160;31, 2006, we have expensed $2.1&#160;million of
    these costs, and we expect the remaining approximately
    $1.7&#160;million to be expensed in 2007. All of the foregoing
    costs are cash outlays. The reduced cost structure resulting
    from implementation of the Plan is expected to provide savings
    of approximately $6.0&#160;million in annual compensation
    expense in 2007 and approximately $7.0&#160;million in annual
    compensation expense in future years.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Under the Plan, we expect to incur additional costs related to
    preparing the site where we will consolidate our development
    activities and related to consolidating our Baltimore
    facilities. At this time, we are unable to make an estimate of
    the expected future savings, associated charges and cash outlays
    resulting from these facility consolidations. We expect that
    these facility consolidations will be completed by the end of
    2007.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Controls
    and Procedures</FONT></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We maintain disclosure controls and procedures, which are
    designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in
    the reports we file or submit under the Securities Exchange Act
    of 1934, as amended, is recorded, processed, summarized and
    reported within the time periods specified in the Securities and
    Exchange Commission&#146;s rules and forms, and that such
    information is accumulated and communicated to our management,
    including our chief executive officer, or CEO, and chief
    financial officer, or CFO, as appropriate to allow timely
    decisions regarding required disclosure.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Under the supervision and with the participation of our
    management, including our CEO and CFO, an evaluation was
    performed on the effectiveness of the design and operation of
    our disclosure controls and procedures as of the end of the
    period covered by this annual report. Based on that evaluation,
    our management, including the CEO and CFO, concluded that our
    disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of
    December&#160;31, 2006. There were no changes in the
    Company&#146;s internal controls over financial reporting during
    the fourth quarter of 2006 that have materially affected or are
    reasonably likely to materially affect the Company&#146;s
    internal control over financial reporting.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    All internal control systems, no matter how well designed, have
    inherent limitations. Therefore, even those systems determined
    to be effective can provide only reasonable assurance with
    respect to financial statement preparation and presentation.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Management&#146;s report on internal control over financial
    reporting is included in Item&#160;8 of this Annual Report on
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">Form&#160;10-K.</FONT>
</DIV>
